title: Potential Outcomes & Average Treatment Effects
interviewAnswer: Causal inference defines treatment effects through potential outcomes: what the same unit would experience under treatment versus control. Because both cannot be observed, identification requires randomization or assumptions/design.
keyPoints: Fundamental problem: one potential outcome is missing.
ATE, ATT and CATE answer different questions.
why: Potential Outcomes & Average Treatment Effects appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Fundamental problem: one potential outcome is missing.
deepDive: Causal inference defines treatment effects through potential outcomes: what the same unit would experience under treatment versus control. Because both cannot be observed, identification requires randomization or assumptions/design. ATE, ATT and CATE answer different questions. Assignment mechanism is central. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Estimate the average effect of a pricing banner, not merely whether exposed users buy more.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Potential Outcomes & Average Treatment Effects make?
How would you validate or debug Potential Outcomes & Average Treatment Effects in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
